Thanks for the clear notes, Sergio. A few quick operational clarifications before the call:

- Available headroom for July 1–14: we can guarantee 30 T4-equivalent reserved slots in the targeted region immediately. We can provision an additional 50 burst-equivalent slots but those require a 24–36 hour prep window for instance spin-up and warm caching.
- NVL/long-context jobs: anything over 6k tokens will trigger longer tail latency and increased KV pressure. Recommend either limiting those demos or scheduling them during low-traffic windows.
- Pre-provisioning: if CloudWave expects sustained demo traffic for >24 hours, we should convert 20 of the burst slots into short-term reserved capacity for predictability. That gives us better SLOs and simplifies billing.

I dropped a short runbook in the Drive (link below) that shows the two-step burst provisioning and the rollback steps. Also attached a PDF 'burst-provisioning-runbook.pdf' for the customer-facing MOP.

Drive: https://drive.redwood/drive/folders/1a2b3c-capacity-lighthouse
